text:
Recommendation: Offer the annual plan at $490/year rather than skipping it. Consider starting with a soft launch to the 40 customers who asked before adding it to the public pricing page.
Why:
- 40 customers (13% of your base) explicitly asked for it, signaling intent to stay long-term and possibly a procurement need for annual invoicing.
- The apparent $98 discount per switcher only holds if that customer would have stayed all 12 months on monthly; if monthly churn is above roughly 3%, annual billing earns more even before counting upfront cash flow (e.g., $19.6k upfront if all 40 switch).
- "Two months free" is standard SaaS annual pricing (roughly 15-20% off), not a brand-damaging discount; brand harm comes from random, frequent, or headline-price cuts, not a permanent annual option.
Risks and unknowns:
- Customers who would have stayed 12+ months anyway now pay $98 less — this is the real cost, and it depends on your actual monthly churn rate.
- You'll need a refund policy for mid-year cancellations (e.g., no refund but access continues until term ends).
- Annual customers won't see a price increase until renewal.
Next steps:
1. Check your current monthly churn rate — above ~3% makes annual billing net positive even ignoring cash flow benefits.
2. Set up Stripe for annual billing (about a day) and decide on a refund/cancellation policy.
3. Email the annual option to the 40 who asked (and possibly your full customer base) before adding it to the public pricing page, then evaluate uptake and churn before making it permanent.
